plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 33: Electromagnetic Waves
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional drawing of a translucent teal rectangular box serving as a Gaussian surface, with electric field vectors drawn at two opposite faces. A small axis key in the upper right shows y pointing up, x pointing right, and z toward the lower left. The box is tall and thin: a bracket along the left edge gives that side as l, a bracket along the top rear edge gives another side as l, and a bracket across the bottom front gives the short third dimension as Δx. Curved leaders name the faces, with Side 2 on the top, Side 1 on the bottom, Side 3 on the near left face, and Side 4 printed in gray on the face beyond. Two identical red vector triads appear, each with one arrow up, one to the right, and one toward the lower left. The left triad is labeled Ey(x,t), Ex(x,t), and Ez(x,t); the right triad, displaced by the thickness of the box, reads Ey(x+Δx,t), Ex(x+Δx,t), and Ez(x+Δx,t), and a dashed line through both origins continues to an arrowhead labeled x. Repeating one triad at two positions along x frames the comparison as flux entering one face against flux leaving the opposite one, the setup for applying Gauss's law to a wave traveling along the x-axis.

elements: Translucent teal rectangular Gaussian box, parameterized by width Δx
Label 'Side 2' with curved leader line pointing to the top face
Label 'Side 1' with curved leader line pointing to the bottom face
Label 'Side 3' printed on the lower-left of the front face
Label 'Side 4' printed in gray on the lower-right of the back face
Dimension bracket and label 'l' along the left vertical edge (height)
Dimension bracket and label 'l' along the top-rear edge (depth)
Dimension bracket and label 'Δx' along the bottom-front edge (width)
Dashed axis line passing through the horizontal center of the box, ending in an arrow labeled 'x'
Left vector triad originating at the center of the left face: three red arrows with labels E_x(x,t), E_y(x,t), E_z(x,t)
Right vector triad originating at the center of the right face: three red arrows with labels E_x(x+Δx,t), E_y(x+Δx,t), E_z(x+Δx,t)
Global coordinate axes indicator at top right showing x, y, z directions

interactions.label: Box Width Δx
interactions.teaches: Widening the box moves the right face further along the x-axis, emphasizing that Gauss's law evaluates the field at two different points along the propagation direction.
Clicking a face highlights its surface and displays its outward normal vector, visually separating which electric field components pierce the face to contribute to net flux.

interactions.label: Show E_x
interactions.teaches: The x-component of the electric field only contributes to flux through the left and right faces, as it is parallel to all other faces.

interactions.label: Show E_y
interactions.teaches: The y-component only pierces Side 1 (bottom) and Side 2 (top), contributing to flux only on those horizontal surfaces.

interactions.label: Show E_z
interactions.teaches: The z-component only pierces Side 3 (front) and Side 4 (back), completely bypassing the other four faces.

demo_steps.title: Full Field Overview
demo_steps.narration: A Gaussian box spans from x to x+Δx. The electric field is evaluated at the center of both the left and right faces, with all three components shown.

demo_steps.title: Transverse Field (Ey)
demo_steps.narration: Isolate the y-component. Because it points vertically, it does not pierce the left or right faces at all—it only contributes to flux through Side 1 and Side 2.

demo_steps.title: Varying Box Width
demo_steps.narration: Increasing Δx extends the box. The right face slides outward, capturing the field E(x+Δx, t) further down the wave's path of propagation.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World dimensions: Box height l=4 (y ∈ [-2,2]), depth l=4 (z ∈ [-2,2]), width Δx controlled by slider (x ∈ [0, Δx]). Box material: transparent teal (#a0d8d8, opacity 0.3) with solid edges. The left face is fixed at x=0; the right face slides to x=Δx. 'Side 2' is the top face (y=2), 'Side 1' is the bottom (y=-2), 'Side 3' is the front (z=2), 'Side 4' is the back (z=-2). Left vector triad originates at (0,0,0); right triad at (Δx,0,0). Field vectors are red (#cc2222) arrows, ~1.5 units long, pointing along +x, +y, +z. Dashed line runs along x-axis (y=0, z=0) from x=-1.5 to x=Δx+1.5. Brackets are black lines with terminal arrows: height bracket offset from x=0, z=2 edge; depth bracket offset from x=0, y=2 edge; width bracket offset from y=-2, z=2 edge.
interactionPlan.notes: Link the position of the right face, right triad, dashed line endpoint, and the width bracket to the deltaX slider. The showEx, showEy, and showEz toggles should independently hide or reveal their respective red vector arrows and labels in both triads. The click interaction uses a raycaster on the six faces; when clicked, briefly animate the face opacity higher and draw a distinct outward normal vector arrow from the center of that face.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for Delta x: the learner widens or narrows the box along the x direction, the two red field triads separate or approach and the difference between E(x,t) and E(x+Delta x,t) updates, showing that Gauss's-law reasoning compares nearby faces along the propagation direction.

authoredContext:
We examine first what Gauss’s law for electric fields implies about the relative directions of the electric field and the propagation direction in an electromagnetic wave. Assume the Gaussian surface to be the surface of a rectangular box whose cross-section is a square of side l and whose third side has length Δx, as shown in the figure. Because the electric field is a function only of x and t, the y-component of the electric field is the same on both the top (labeled Side 2) and bottom (labeled Side 1) of the box, so that these two contributions to the flux cancel. The corresponding argument also holds for the net flux from the z-component of the electric field through Sides 3 and 4. Any net flux through the surface therefore comes entirely from the x-component of the electric field. Because the electric field has no y- or z-dependence, Ex(x,t) is constant over the face of the box with area A and has a possibly different value Ex(x+Δx,t) that is constant over the opposite face of the box. Applying Gauss’s law gives

where A=l×l is the area of the front and back faces of the rectangular surface. But the charge enclosed is Qin=0, so this component’s net flux is also zero, and the equation implies Ex(x,t)=Ex(x+Δx,t) for any Δx. Therefore, if there is an x-component of the electric field, it cannot vary with x. A uniform field of that kind would merely be superposed artificially on the traveling wave, for example, by having a pair of parallel-charged plates. Such a component Ex(x,t) would not be part of an electromagnetic wave propagating along the x-axis; so Ex(x,t)=0 for this wave. Therefore, the only nonzero components of the electric field are Ey(x,t) and Ez(x,t), perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the wave.

The surface of a rectangular box of dimensions l×l×Δx is our Gaussian surface. The electric field shown is from an electromagnetic wave propagating along the x-axis.

Figure shows a rectangular box of dimensions l by l by delta x. The top and bottom sides, parallel to the xz plane are labeled side 2 and side 1 respectively. The front and back sides, parallel to the xy plane are labeled side 3 and side 4 respectively. Three arrows originate from a point on the left side. These are along the x, y and z axis and are respectively labeled E subscript x parentheses x, t parentheses, E subscript y parentheses x, t parentheses and E subscript z parentheses x, t parentheses. Three more arrows originate from the point where the x axis intersects the right side of the box. These, too, are along the the x, y and z axis and are respectively labeled E subscript x parentheses x plus delta x, t parentheses, E subscript y parentheses x plus delta x, t parentheses and E subscript z parentheses x plus delta x, t parentheses.

A similar argument holds by substituting E for B and using Gauss’s law for magnetism instead of Gauss’s law for electric fields. This shows that the B field is also perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the wave. The electromagnetic wave is therefore a transverse wave, with its oscillating electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to its direction of propagation.

Demo Scenarios:
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The camera view angle is incorrect; the depth (z-axis) goes up-left instead of into the page (right-up), viewing the box from the opposite side.
The field vector labels (E_x, E_y, E_z) on the triads heavily overlap each other, particularly on the right face.
The dimension bracket for depth 'l' is placed on the top-left edge going up-left, whereas the source has it on the top-front edge going right-up.
The 'Side 3' and 'Side 4' labels are placed floating at the bottom in the generated figure, rather than being centered on their respective faces.
The generated figure faces are rendered with a heavily visible teal fill, whereas the source figure is mostly transparent with very faint shading.
evaluation.notes: The interactive features are outstanding and explain the core concept well, but the figure is viewed from the wrong octant (reversing the depth direction) and suffers from severe label overlapping.
action_items: Adjust the camera view (e.g., modifying axisScreenAngles) so that the +x axis goes right-down and the +z axis goes left-down (with -z going right-up into the page) to match the source perspective.
Increase the positional offsets for the E_x, E_y, and E_z labels on both triads so they do not overlap each other.
Position the 'Side 3' and 'Side 4' labels at the physical centers of the front and back faces.
Lower the opacity of the face materials to 0.1 or 0.15 to better match the highly transparent look of the source box.

feedback.rationale: The conceptual structure and interactivity are excellent, but there are several execution-level issues like incorrect camera angle, overlapping labels, and material opacity that the generator needs to fix.

Adjust the HTML offsets for the right-side electric field labels to prevent overlap with the arrows.
Change the dimension bracket arrows to point inwards toward the ticks rather than outwards.

discrepancies: The dashed line representing the x-axis extends behind the left face in the generated figure, whereas it starts exactly at the left face center in the source.
The 'Side 3' label is centered on the front face instead of placed in the bottom-left corner, causing minor visual clutter.
The dimension brackets have arrows pointing outwards from the endpoints instead of inwards towards the ticks.
Some electric field labels (especially on the right face) overlap slightly with the arrow heads and box edges.
gemini-3.1-pro.notes: Excellent pedagogical interactive features with accurate 3D geometry; minor discrepancies in the dashed line extent and label positioning.
